newsitem.title: FRANCE: Boeing hopes for merger approvals in summer.
newsitem.headline: Boeing hopes for merger approvals in summer.

text.p: Boeing hopes its planned merger with McDonnell Douglas will obtain the necessary approvals this summer, chairman and chief executive Philip Condit said in a French newspaper interview published on Monday.

"If the merger is authorised by the relevant administrations -- and we hope it will be this summer -- we expect little restructuring this year. The real savings will be generated in 1998 and could reach $1 billion," he told Le Figaro.
"We hope to improve our profit this year and we don't expect to be in deficit even for a second because of this merger," he said.
The merger requires clearances from the European Union and U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
Condit said the merger would drive Boeing toward its "ideal" 50-50 split between civilian and defence aircraft sales.

"The merger with McDonnell Douglas will give us a major boost, with 60 percent of our activity in the civilian market and 40 percent in defence and space. That's a split that approaches our ideal of 50-50," he said.
In the civilian market, Condit said he expected the market shares held by Boeing and its European rival Airbus to remain stable in the next few years.
"I also think the price war will continue. That's why Boeing needs to be even more efficient and strive for more productivity gains," said Condit, who is also chief executive.

"The group needs to become more international, that is to say, seek more partnerships and sub-contractors outside the United States. We're calling on British Aerospace or CASA (Construcciones Aeronauticas SA) to supply parts for the 777, while we're making doors for Airbus. Japan represents 20 percent of the manufacturing for the 777 and 25 percent for the 767," he said.
He said Boeing had also forged links with firms in Russia and the Ukraine where technological capacities were high.
